dedupe_keys.name: university of new hampshire water balance model

description: The University of New Hampshire Water Balance Model is a gridded hydrological model released by its Water Systems Analysis Group. Its public repository contains the Perl model, the RIMS library, configuration files and a list of output variables. Utilities prepare binary inputs, subset digital river networks and aggregate model outputs in space and time. Spatial coverage is global to regional, with simulation periods and resolution selected through inputs and configuration. Code is free under GPL-3.0, and the linked university site provides ancillary data and a Singularity environment for the published release. These resources can support water-availability and irrigation-demand simulations that inform water infrastructure studies. A limitation is that other research groups maintain development versions that can differ from this release, as the own README warns. The ancillary input collection is a separate reusable dataset and must retain its documented directory structure. This review checked documentation and access links without downloading the container or running the model.
inputs: River network, soil and crop parameters
name: University of New Hampshire Water Balance Model
